name: Animal Collective
discourse_profile: Getting lost as creative method — both making and listening. Portner frames their goal as 'creating something that people can get lost in by getting lost in the environment where we're creating it.' From the outset they refused the band-leader model: 'We didn't want there to be a band leader. We didn't want all the ideas coming from one specific place. We wanted to be diverse and not easy to pinpoint.' Non-repetition is discipline — each record deliberately departs from the last, and Portner actively resists routine: 'If I have a routine going that becomes too familiar to me, I don't want to carry that over into whatever I'm going to cook up with Animal Collective.' Dadaism and Cubism are explicit reference points — taking familiar things out of context, stitching elements into songs where you wouldn't expect them. Vocals function as interlocking organisms: 'two voices become one — without one singer it doesn't really work the same way, they dance with each other.' Sung Tongs tried to make acoustic guitars 'sound electronic' through light touch and microtonal harmonics; Merriweather sampled the band playing acoustic instruments and rebuilt the songs from those loops. Portner insists the process remain organic — 'improvisation is always a tough thing to integrate with computers and modern technology. Gotta keep the organic flow of everything going' — and resists past-oriented creation: 'It's hard for me to make something that's based on the past as opposed to focusing on present feeling and emotion.'
